objectives: 促進國際交流提升本校美國大學知名度，也可提升本校學生前沿生化領域修課多樣性，同時讓中大學生了解美國頂尖學府教學方式且能有效提升學生英文聽力與書寫能力。
content: Drug DesignOverview of how to identify and optimize drugs against a validated biological target (e.g., a protein like HIV protease). Students should have completed a course in Biochemistry (or please contact me). Graduate students are exempt. Each student will generate their own drug design project and poster. There is no text for the course; we will make use of primary research papers, taped lectures, online homework assignments, and zoom sessions to discuss any problems.What are the major reasons for the failure of drugs in clinical trials?How to exploit drug metabolism in drug design.How to use drug delivery to enhance therapeutic index.How to use informatics to screen real and virtual librariesHow to dock candidate inhibitors into target binding sites週次 授課內容 授課方式1 Introduction 面授2 Target Validation 遠距3 Reversible and irreversible enzyme inhibition 遠距4 Quantitative structure-function relationships 遠距5 Pharmacokinetics 遠距6 Combinatorial libraries, high throughput screening 遠距7 Guest speakers from biotechnology and drug companies 遠距8 Combinatorial libraries, high throughput screening 遠距9 Midterm 面授10 Proteins as therapeutics 遠距11 Chem-informatics 遠距12 Medicinal chemistry (SBDD, etc.) 遠距13 Toxicology 遠距14 Drug metabolism 遠距15 Pharmacogenetics/epigenetics 遠距16 Patent law 遠距17 Nucleic acids as therapeutics 遠距18 Final 面授
books: 每週均有期刊論文與輔助教材閱讀
grading_policy: Part of your grade comes from your answering questions based on the five seminars listed below, all on topics of high relevance to this course. Dr. Mike Varney, Head Genentech Research and early development “Discovery and Development of GDC-0032: A Mutant Selective, Beta-Sparing PI3K Inhibitor” Prof. Michelle Arkin, UCSF School of Pharmacy, drug discovery “Inhibiting Protein-Protein Interactions: projections and reflections” Dr. Stacie Canan, Celgene, Executive Director Global Health Division Dr. Dan Shoemaker, Chief Science Officer, Fate Therapeutics “Using Small Molecules to Generate Programmed Cellular Immunotherapies for Fighting Cancer” Dr. Siegfried Reich, Senior VP Research, eFFECTOR Therapeutics
